name: Estádio do Dragão
short: FC Porto's 50,033-seat home stadium, opened in 2003; a UEFA Euro 2004 venue and host of the 2021 Champions League final.
long: Estádio do Dragão (Dragon Stadium) is the home ground of FC Porto, built on the site of the old Estádio das Antas for UEFA Euro 2004. It was designed by the architect Manuel Salgado and opened on 16 November 2003. It seats 50,033 and is a UEFA category four stadium. Its frame is clad in around 21,000 square metres of azulejo tiles.
history:
Construction began in late 2001 and was completed in November 2003, replacing the former Estádio das Antas. The design is by the architect Manuel Salgado, the contractor was Somague, and the cost was about 125 million euros.

The inauguration took place on 16 November 2003 in a friendly against Barcelona: Porto won 2–0 with goals from Derlei and Hugo Almeida. The attendance of 52,004 remains the stadium record.

Turf problems forced Porto to briefly return to the old Estádio das Antas until the pitch was relaid in February 2004. The name Dragão was chosen after the dragon in the club's and the city's coat of arms.

In summer 2004 the stadium hosted the opening match of UEFA Euro 2004, in which Portugal lost 1–2 to Greece, plus four more tournament games including a quarter-final and a semi-final.

It later hosted the 2019 UEFA Nations League Final (Portugal 1–0 Netherlands) and the 2021 UEFA Champions League Final (Chelsea beat Manchester City). The arena also stages concerts and other events.
facts: Opened on 16 November 2003; the home ground of FC Porto.
Capacity of 50,033; it is a UEFA category four (elite) stadium.
Designed by the architect Manuel Salgado, built by Somague, at a cost of about 125 million euros.
Record attendance of 52,004 at the match against Barcelona on 16 November 2003.
Its frame is clad in around 21,000 square metres of azulejo tiles.
Hosted the UEFA Euro 2004 opening match (Portugal 1–2 Greece) and the 2021 Champions League final.
It has its own metro station, Estádio do Dragão, with a direct line to the airport.
tip: The exterior is best seen from the main facade; check the FC Porto museum and stadium tour times at fcporto.pt. The easiest way to arrive is the metro to Estádio do Dragão station.
